page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system includes 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. The network configuration delivers a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, showing strong results in both cached small-block reads at 4502.68 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 215.93 GB/sec. Single-core performance is comparatively weaker, as seen in stress-ng single-core and gzip single-threaded compression tests. The instance excels in high-throughput database operations, achieving 75.03 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 44.7 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given the high density of DDR4 memory, integrated NVMe storage, and 100 Gbps networking, this instance offers a resource-dense profile for memory-intensive and network-bound workloads. It is well-suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, high-throughput web serving, and software compilation tasks. However, it is less optimal for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance or GPU-accelerated computing.
